enzyme_name: none for this half-step (spontaneous imine hydrolysis); dehydrospermidine is generated by spermidine dehydrogenase (SpdH, EC 1.5.99.6) or by FAD/Cu amine oxidases
organism_context: Citrobacter freundii / Pseudomonas spp. (SpdH); plant and bacterial polyamine oxidases generate the same imine
rationale: Dehydrospermidine is the Schiff-base (imine) released by spermidine dehydrogenase/polyamine oxidase; its breakdown to 4-aminobutanal + 1,3-diaminopropane is the spontaneous aqueous hydrolysis of that imine, so no protein catalyses this MetaCyc half-reaction. Calling it 'monofunctional' would mis-assign the oxidase's activity to a non-enzymatic step.
direction_note: Imine hydrolysis in bulk water is strongly favoured; the ModelSEED '<' direction would require condensing free 4-aminobutanal with 1,3-diaminopropane, which is not a metabolic step.

enzyme_name: mitomycin O-carbamoyltransferase (MmcS)
organism_context: Streptomyces lavendulae / S. caespitosus mitomycin biosynthetic cluster
rationale: The carbamoylation of the C10 hydroxymethyl of the 9beta-mitosane core is the single tailoring step assigned to the cluster-encoded carbamoyltransferase MmcS; it is a one-activity group-transfer enzyme. Enzyme identity is inferred from the pathway context rather than from a dedicated MmcS characterisation paper.
direction_note: Carbamoyl transfer from carbamoyl phosphate with release of Pi is strongly exergonic and biosynthetically unidirectional; the ModelSEED '<' call rests on a bronze-grade dGPredictor estimate for an exotic mitosane.

enzyme_name: glutathione peroxidase (GPX4 / phospholipid hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase; GPX1 for free hydroperoxy fatty acids)
organism_context: mammalian; GPX4 is the selenoenzyme that reduces free and esterified polyunsaturated fatty acid hydroperoxides
rationale: Reduction of 14(S)-HpDHA to 14(S)-HDoHE at the expense of 2 GSH is the standard selenocysteine glutathione-peroxidase reaction; GPx enzymes carry a single catalytic (thioredoxin-fold) active site. Enzyme class is known with confidence; the specific isoform for this substrate is not pinned.
direction_note: The GSSG product is missing from the ModelSEED equation (status MI:C:-20/H:-27/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2, i.e. exactly one glutathione disulfide), so every thermodynamic estimate behind the '<' call is computed on a broken equation; peroxide reduction itself is irreversible.

enzyme_name: unknown; thiol-disulfide exchange on S-(methylsulfanyl)glutathione, possibly spontaneous or glutaredoxin-catalysed
rationale: Release of methanethiol from the mixed disulfide GS-S-CH3 by a second GSH is ordinary thiol-disulfide exchange; no catalysing protein could be identified and such exchanges proceed non-enzymatically or via glutaredoxin. Searching the compound name returned no literature.
direction_note: GSSG is absent from the products (MI short exactly one glutathione disulfide); and thiol-disulfide exchange has no intrinsic direction - it is set by the cellular GSH/GSSG ratio, not by an enzyme.

enzyme_name: beta-D-glucosidase acting on flavonoid 7-O-beta-D-glucosides (apigenin 7-O-glucosidase)
organism_context: plant / gut-microbial GH1-type beta-glucosidases; the specific protein behind MetaCyc RXN-22893 was not identified
rationale: Hydrolysis of cosmosiin (apigenin 7-O-beta-D-glucoside) to apigenin + glucose is a one-active-site glycoside hydrolase reaction; GH1 beta-glucosidases are single-domain monofunctional enzymes. The particular protein MetaCyc assigns was not pinned down (MetaCyc is unreachable from this environment).
direction_note: ModelSEED's '<' would run the reaction as condensation of free D-glucose with apigenin; glycosidases do not do that physiologically (O-glycosylation uses UDP-glucose), so only the hydrolytic direction is enzymologically real.

enzyme_name: 1,4-dihydroxy-6-naphthoate synthase (MqnD; also named 5,8-dihydroxy-2-naphthoate synthase)
organism_context: futalosine (alternative menaquinone) pathway in Streptomyces, Thermus, Helicobacter, Campylobacter
rationale: MqnD converts cyclic dehypoxanthinyl futalosine into 1,4-dihydroxy-6-naphthoate with loss of the C3 sugar fragment (glycerone); it is a single-activity lyase with one active site. Mechanism characterised by Manion-Sommerhalter et al.
direction_note: Aromatisation of the naphthalenediol makes the MqnD step effectively irreversible in the biosynthetic direction; the reverse would require re-adding glycerone to an aromatic ring.

enzyme_name: beta-D-glucosidase acting on flavonoid O-beta-D-glucosides (luteolin 4'-O-glucosidase)
organism_context: plant / gut-microbial GH1-type beta-glucosidases; the specific protein behind MetaCyc RXN-22890 was not identified
rationale: Same chemistry and same enzyme class as rxn58985 and rxn59479: a single-active-site glycoside hydrolase releasing D-glucose from the 4'-O-glucoside of luteolin. Specific catalysing protein not pinned.
direction_note: The ModelSEED '<' direction is a glucose + aglycone condensation, which is not what any glycoside hydrolase does in vivo.

enzyme_name: unknown tetraether-backbone methyltransferase (probable radical SAM enzyme converting BDGT to PDGT)
organism_context: Methanomassiliicoccus luminyensis; BDGT/PDGT lipids also found in anoxic subseafloor sediments
rationale: Coffinet et al. showed by [methyl-13C]methionine labelling that BDGT/PDGT arise by methyl transfer from SAM onto the GDGT backbone, but explicitly state the enzyme is unidentified and that a radical SAM mechanism is only probable because the target is an unactivated methylene.
direction_note: A radical SAM methylation of a methylene releases 5'-deoxyadenosine + L-methionine, not SAH; writing it as SAM -> SAH abstracts away the cofactor chemistry that makes the step irreversible, but methyl transfer still only runs toward the methylated lipid.

enzyme_name: unknown ATP-dependent acyl-adenylate-forming (adenylating) enzyme acting on 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate
rationale: The chemistry is unambiguous (acyl-adenylate formation from ATP + a 2-oxo acid with PPi release), but no literature search returned the protein or pathway that makes (3-methyl-2-oxobutanoyl)adenylate, so the catalysing enzyme and its domain architecture are genuinely unknown.
direction_note: Acyl-adenylates are transient activated intermediates: metabolic flux runs toward the adenylate (pulled by pyrophosphatase and by the downstream acyl transfer), even though the reverse PPi-ATP exchange is readily demonstrable in vitro.

enzyme_name: ClbS, colibactin cyclopropane hydrolase (colibactin self-resistance protein)
organism_context: pks-island-carrying Escherichia coli
rationale: Tripathi et al. showed ClbS hydrolytically opens the cyclopropane (spirobicyclic) warheads of colibactin, inactivating it; that is its single catalytic activity. ClbS also binds DNA (Molan et al.), but a protective nucleic-acid-binding role is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Hydrolytic opening of a strained cyclopropane is irreversible; the ModelSEED '<' direction would re-form two cyclopropanes from the diol and expel water, which does not happen.

enzyme_name: arabinofuranosyltransferase EmbA/EmbB (decaprenylphosphoryl-arabinose-dependent GT-C glycosyltransferase)
organism_context: Mycobacterium tuberculosis / M. smegmatis arabinogalactan assembly; the ethambutol target
rationale: Arabinan extension of the arabinogalactan is carried out by the Emb arabinosyltransferases, each a single-activity polyprenyl-phosphosugar glycosyltransferase (EmbB cryo-EM structure, Tan et al.). EmbA and EmbB work as an associated pair - that is a multi-subunit assembly, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: The two polymer pseudo-compounds differ by far more than the six transferred arabinofuranoses (status MI:C:-135/H:-216/O:-108), so this is a placeholder equation; the underlying glycosyl transfer from DPA with release of decaprenyl phosphate is nevertheless irreversible in the biosynthetic direction.

enzyme_name: SAM-dependent sugar C-3 methyltransferase acting on dTDP-4-oxo-L-rhamnose (TylC3/EvaC/NovU-type branched-sugar C-methyltransferase)
organism_context: actinomycete deoxysugar (3-C-methyl branched sugar) biosynthesis; the specific protein behind MetaCyc RXN-23238 was not identified
rationale: Installing a 3-C-methyl branch on a dTDP-4-keto-6-deoxy sugar is the hallmark reaction of the TylC3/EvaC/NovU family of standalone SAM-dependent C-methyltransferases, all single-activity enzymes. The exact protein for this substrate was not confirmed in the literature search.
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer onto carbon is effectively irreversible; the ModelSEED '<' call would demethylate a C-methyl group using SAH, which no methyltransferase does.

enzyme_name: glutathione peroxidase (GPX4 / GPX1) acting on 12(S)-HPETE
organism_context: mammalian; reduction of the 12-lipoxygenase product 12(S)-HPETE to 12(S)-HETE
rationale: Single-active-site selenocysteine glutathione peroxidase reducing a fatty acid hydroperoxide to the corresponding alcohol; GPx enzymes are monofunctional. Isoform assignment for this particular substrate is not pinned.
direction_note: GSSG is missing from the products (MI short exactly one glutathione disulfide), so the '<' recommendation rests on a thermodynamic estimate of a non-reaction; peroxide reduction is chemically irreversible.

enzyme_name: N5-methyltetrahydromethanopterin:coenzyme M methyltransferase (Mtr), Na+-translocating MtrA-H complex
organism_context: methanogenic archaea (Methanosarcina, Methanothermobacter) and ANME archaea
rationale: Mtr is an eight-subunit membrane complex: MtrH transfers the methyl group to the MtrA corrinoid and thence to CoM, with MtrE/MtrD coupling Na+ translocation. Separate polypeptides in a complex are explicitly not a fused bifunctional enzyme, so the catalytic subunit is monofunctional.
direction_note: Methyl-CoM, the methyl acceptor product, is simply absent from the equation (MI:C:-3/H:-8/O:-3/S:-2 = exactly one methyl-CoM); and Mtr is a genuinely reversible Na+ pump - it runs toward methyl-CoM in hydrogenotrophic/acetoclastic methanogenesis and in reverse in ANME archaea and in methylotrophic methanogens oxidising methyl groups to CO2, so direction is set by the Na+ gradient and the methyl pools, not by the enzyme.

enzyme_name: unknown (7-methoxy -> 7-amino exchange); MmcR is the adjacent mitomycin 7-O-methyltransferase that makes mitomycin A, not this step
organism_context: Streptomyces lavendulae mitomycin pathway
rationale: Singh et al. show MmcR 7-O-methylates 7-hydroxymitomycins to give mitomycin A, so MmcR cannot be the catalyst of the A -> C conversion; no enzyme is established for replacing the 7-methoxy by an amino group, and amines displace the 7-OMe of mitomycin A readily enough that the step may be non-enzymatic.
direction_note: Ammonia in and methanol out are both missing (status MI:C:-1/H:-1/N:1/O:-1), so the written 1:1 conversion cannot be balanced; chemically mitomycin A (7-OMe, made by MmcR) must be the precursor and mitomycin C (7-NH2) the product, matching the LLM's direction.

enzyme_name: unknown
rationale: No literature could be found for the interconversion of dipicolinate (pyridine-2,6-dicarboxylate, C7) and 2,3-dihydroxypicolinate (C6), and no EC number or gene is attached; the catalysing enzyme is genuinely unidentified.
direction_note: The two compounds differ by a carbon and two oxygens (status MI:C:-1/H:1|CI:1): any real conversion would need O2, a reductant and CO2 release, so neither written direction is a meaningful statement of the chemistry.

enzyme_name: glutathione-cystine transhydrogenase (EC 1.8.4.4); in practice the glutaredoxin/thioltransferase (GLRX) activity
organism_context: mammalian cytosol (rat/bovine liver and lens thioltransferase)
rationale: EC 1.8.4.4 is still a live IUBMB/KEGG entry (glutathione-cystine transhydrogenase, confirmed by the KEGG enzyme record) and the activity is carried by small single-domain glutaredoxins with one CXXC active site; deglutathionylation and dithiol reduction are the same chemistry, not two activities.
direction_note: GSSG is missing from the product side (MI short exactly one glutathione disulfide); and a transhydrogenase is an exchange catalyst with no intrinsic direction - the cytosolic GSH/GSSG ratio, not the protein, decides whether cystine is reduced or cysteine oxidised.

enzyme_name: none - four enzymes: LmbM (6-epimerase), LmbL (6,8-dehydratase), CcbZ/LmbZ (4-epimerase) and CcbS/LmbS (PLP-dependent 6-transaminase)
organism_context: Streptomyces lincolnensis (lincomycin A) and S. caelestis (celesticetin)
rationale: Wang et al. showed that GDP-D-erythro-alpha-D-gluco-octose is converted to GDP-D-alpha-D-lincosamide by four separate enzymes performing 6-epimerisation, 6,8-dehydration, 4-epimerisation and 6-transamination, so no single enzyme catalyses the ModelSEED entry and no functionality class applies to it.
direction_note: Four steps are collapsed into one entry (and the transaminase's amino donor is absent, hence MI:H:3/N:1/O:-2), so the '<' thermodynamic call is meaningless; the pathway flux runs octose -> lincosamide, matching the LLM.

enzyme_name: unknown (formation of ACNQ from 1,4-dihydroxy-2-naphthoate)
organism_context: Propionibacterium freudenreichii; ACNQ acts as a bifidogenic extracellular electron mediator
rationale: ACNQ (2-amino-3-carboxy-1,4-naphthoquinone) is the well-studied bifidus growth stimulator derived from DHNA, but the literature characterises only its redox-mediator function, not a catalysing enzyme; no protein is assigned to the amination/oxidation.
direction_note: The nitrogen donor and the two-electron oxidation of the hydroquinone to the quinone are both absent (MI:H:-1/N:1); DHNA is nevertheless the precursor and ACNQ the product, so the LLM's direction is the right one.

enzyme_name: none for the single step - NAD(P)H-dependent anthrol/anthraquinone reductase (MdpK/AflM-type) plus a dehydration/tautomerisation
organism_context: fungal anthraquinone/xanthone pathways (Aspergillus nidulans monodictyphenone, agnestin cluster)
rationale: The reductive route from emodin to chrysophanol runs through emodin hydroquinone made by an NAD(P)H-dependent anthrol reductase, followed by dehydration/tautomerisation - two steps, so the single ModelSEED entry has no one catalysing enzyme (the reductase itself is monofunctional).
direction_note: NAD(P)H (and the released water) are missing, and it is precisely the reductant that makes the deoxygenation irreversible; biosynthesis runs emodin -> chrysophanol, matching the LLM.

enzyme_name: glutathione peroxidase (GPX4 / GPX1) acting on 5(S)-HpEPE
organism_context: mammalian; reduction of the EPA-derived 5-lipoxygenase hydroperoxide to 5(S)-HEPE
rationale: Same single-active-site selenocysteine glutathione peroxidase chemistry as rxn58957 and rxn59144, applied to the eicosapentaenoate hydroperoxide; GPx enzymes carry one catalytic activity.
direction_note: GSSG is absent from the products (MI short exactly one glutathione disulfide), so the '<' recommendation is derived from a broken equation; the peroxidase step itself is irreversible.

enzyme_name: phlorizin hydrolase - in mammals one of the two active sites of lactase-phlorizin hydrolase (LPH)
distinct_activities: phlorizin hydrolase / glycosyl-N-acylsphingosine glucohydrolase (EC 3.2.1.62), on domain IV
organism_context: mammalian intestinal brush border (single LCT gene product); plant and microbial phlorizin-cleaving beta-glucosidases are separate monofunctional GH1 enzymes
rationale: LPH is a single polypeptide carrying two chemically distinct, separately mutable glycosidase active sites (lactase and phlorizin hydrolase/glycosylceramidase), demonstrated by differential inhibition and by domain mapping. Bifunctionality is certain for LPH; it is less certain that MetaCyc RXN-22887 refers to LPH rather than to a plant beta-glucosidase.
direction_note: Both of LPH's activities are hydrolytic and run in the same (glycoside-cleaving) direction, so the bifunctionality does not explain the conflict; ModelSEED's '<' is a glucose + phloretin condensation that no glycosidase performs in vivo.

enzyme_name: unknown (hydrolysis of the allysine-fructosamine Schiff base; glycation-type chemistry, probably spontaneous)
rationale: The substrate is simply the imine formed between the aldehyde of allysine (2-aminoadipate 6-semialdehyde) and the amine of free fructosamine; no catalysing protein was found in the literature and such imine hydrolyses are typically non-enzymatic.
direction_note: In dilute aqueous solution an aliphatic aldimine hydrolyses rather than forms, so the hydrolytic direction the LLM chose is the favoured one; the ModelSEED '<' rests on a disputed bronze-grade estimate.

enzyme_name: unknown / spontaneous dehydration; the preceding C5 hydroxylation is done by a CYP81A-family cytochrome P450 of cocaine biosynthesis
organism_context: Erythroxylum coca tropane alkaloid (cocaine) pathway
rationale: Chavez et al. identified a CYP81A P450 that effects the second tropane ring closure via hydroxylation of 4-(1-methyl-2-pyrrolidinyl)-3-oxobutanoate; the carbinolamine-to-N-methyl-Delta1-pyrrolinium dehydration written here is the uncatalysed equilibrium step between that hydroxylation and the intramolecular Mannich cyclisation, with no enzyme assigned.
direction_note: Pathway flux runs carbinolamine -> iminium -> tropane ring, so the LLM's direction is the on-pathway one, but the isolated hydration/dehydration equilibrium may well favour the carbinolamine (eQuilibrator +7.7 kJ/mol); it is the downstream irreversible cyclisation that pulls it forward.

enzyme_name: MccB, microcin C7 adenylyltransferase (ThiF/MoeB-family ancestor of the ubiquitin E1 enzymes)
organism_context: Escherichia coli microcin C7 (MccA heptapeptide) biosynthesis
rationale: Regni et al. showed MccB carries out two successive ATP-dependent adenylations of the MccA C-terminal asparagine (succinimide formation, then phosphoramidate formation) in one active site; two rounds of the same adenylyl-transfer chemistry are one catalytic activity, not two.
direction_note: Adenylation with PPi release is the physiological half-reaction and is pulled forward by pyrophosphatase and by the subsequent intramolecular attack; the ModelSEED '<' would run peptidyl-adenylate + PPi back to ATP.
